findings.title: Adapter selection is parsed twice: an ad-hoc argv scan picks the collector, clap's parse names it in the summary
findings.evidence: crates/cli/src/sessions.rs:52 requested_session_adapter scans argv independently so crates/app/src/adapters.rs can build the collector before parsing, while the export summary's adapter field comes from clap. They cannot disagree on any clap-accepted invocation today - both take the last occurrence and both accept the = form - so this is drift risk, not a present defect. A future adapter-affecting flag, allow_hyphen_values, or a positional form could let the summary name a different adapter than the one that mapped. Smallest fix if that day comes: expose the composed adapter's name() through CollectionApi and report that instead of the parsed string. Disposition: accepted - the seam is inherent to selecting an implementation before parsing, the obligation is documented at both ends, and the app-registry test exercises the real path.

findings.title: Unmapped top-level native fields are dropped without a diagnostic
findings.evidence: crates/adapter-claude/src/lib.rs reads only type, uuid, parentUuid, sessionId, isSidechain, timestamp and message; toolUseResult, cwd, gitBranch, version, requestId and userType are neither exported nor counted, and only invalid recognised fields raise InvalidField. Disposition: accepted - this is the documented projection boundary, not a defect. docs/claude-adapter.md states outer toolUseResult is not interpreted or exported, and docs/fidelity.md classifies complete unknown-field retention as unsupported behavior. Treating it as a gate would contradict the operator's recorded decision that fidelity is a delivery report, not new scope.

findings.title: A test reports green on this filesystem while proving nothing
findings.evidence: crates/loader-jsonl/tests/filesystem.rs:161 non_utf8_candidates_are_rejected_when_filesystem_permits_them passes on APFS by printing a NOT EXERCISED notice when fs::write returns EILSEQ, so a reader counting passing tests could over-read platform coverage. Disposition: accepted - the alternatives are worse, since a hard failure would break the lane on the developer platform and #[ignore] would hide it. The limitation is disclosed in three places (the stderr notice, tk-0002-validation-corrected.json and fidelity.md), and the before-I/O non-UTF-8 rejection path is genuinely exercised by non_utf8_roots_and_inputs_are_rejected_before_io.

findings.title: encode_value recursion depth is a caller obligation, not a writer bound
findings.evidence: crates/output-otlp/src/lib.rs:123 recurses per nesting level; the 32 MiB cap does not bound stack depth because each level writes only about 24 bytes. Disposition: accepted - unreachable on the shipped path, because records arrive through serde_json::from_slice at default features (1.0.151, no unbounded_depth) so input nesting is capped by the deserializer long before the writer sees it. Only an in-process injected adapter constructing a Value directly could exceed it, which is the same trust domain as the composition root. If a hostile-adapter threat model is ever adopted, add a depth counter in encode_value returning InvalidData.
